quorum.judges_note: judges=3 counts the three lanes asked per round, across three rounds; it is not three independent tiers. ONE REFUTATION (R8) CAME FROM MEASURING A LANE'S OWN HAND-TRACE: round 3's Claude lane reported a `&&` chain as classified correctly, and adding it as an asserted case failed at once. The lane that found the value-flag defect also asserted a false negative was fine. Neither family was reliable alone in round 3; the defence was turning every trace into an asserted case.
quorum.kill_rule: nothing was dismissed. Each round's findings were fixed rather than argued with, and the rounds stopped after three not because agreement was reached but because each round now finds the next edge of a heuristic shell parser. The residual limits — arguments hidden in a shell variable, or split across a backslash continuation — are stated in the commit message rather than chased; no workflow in the tree uses either for a test invocation.
refuted_claims: R1: 'four declared mutations' — the file declared one. All three round-1 lanes, independently. Every mutation is now declared in the file header.

R2: pinning kani, lean and coverage was complete — stress.yml (`cargo test --lib -- --test-threads=1`) and mutation.yml (`cargo mutants`, whose baseline runs the suite) reach the same rsync-requiring test on the same label set. Neither had ever landed on yoga; the lottery was live, undrawn.
R3: 'yoga-build/-build2/-build3' as the present fleet — ephemeral; only yoga-build3 was registered at round 1. Now stated as ephemeral and observed on 2026-09-20.

R4: the substring detector — missed bare `cargo test`, `--workspace`, `--all-targets`, `cargo nextest run`, `--locked --lib`. False negatives, the dangerous direction. Two lanes independently. Tokenized.
R5: stopping at `--` — a name filter after the separator was classed unfiltered. The test binary's arguments are now read too.
R6: 'every declared mutation reddens exactly its own arm' — mutation 4 reddens both anti-vacuity floors by design. The file already said so; the claim did not.

R7: round 2's post-separator fix read a libtest flag's VALUE (`--skip slow`) as a name filter, classing a run as narrowed although `--skip` excludes and the run still reaches the safety test. A false negative introduced by the fix for the previous one.

R8: a lane's report that `cargo test --lib && cargo test --doc` classified correctly — measured, the tokenizer read `&&` as a positional filter and called the unfiltered first command narrowed. Lines are now split on shell separators.
R9: 'split across four functions' — true when written, stale after later edits added three. The sentence no longer gives a count.

crux.verdict: No crux row is owed: CI configuration only, no shipped behaviour and no CHANGELOG bullet. Recorded because the design question is real.
systems: Bazel: remote execution selects workers by declared execution properties — a capability, not a hostname [X]; the interim here uses a hostname and names that as its coupling, with a capability label as the done_when
Kubernetes: a pod schedules onto nodes by label selectors and taints against declared capabilities [X], which is the shape infra's capability label would give these jobs
Nix: a build's toolchain is in its input closure, so which prover ran is not ambient runner state [X] — the failure class this interim routes around cannot arise there
